key_idea: C and K are interchangeable, so the count is the number of (A before non-A) inversions; one adjacent swap lowers it by at most 1 and by exactly 1 whenever it is positive.
sketch: Count pairs (A, later C/K) in one pass with a running count of A's. An adjacent swap changes the inversion count by at most one, and while the count is positive some adjacent 'A then C/K' exists and swapping it removes exactly one. Answer max(0, inv - M). O(n). Pitfall: inv is up to 1e10, so use 64-bit.
